subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load

question: Should OpenClaw allow normal auth-store runtime loads to import legacy secret-bearing `auth-profiles.json` into SQLite, or keep that recovery inside doctor/startup migration boundaries?
rationale: The user-facing upgrade failure is real, but choosing runtime fallback versus a doctor/startup migration changes the credential security and compatibility boundary and cannot be safely inferred from code alone.

options.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
options.body: Move the recovery to doctor or an explicit one-shot startup/update migration and keep normal auth reads from consuming retired JSON.

options.title: Approve Runtime Fallback Explicitly
options.body: Accept the runtime import only with maintainer-approved docs, invariant-test changes, and security expectations for retired credential JSON.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: Pause or close this PR if runtime fallback is not desired while a narrower doctor/startup migration fix is prepared.

recommendation.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
recommendation.body: Move the recovery to doctor or an explicit one-shot startup/update migration and keep normal auth reads from consuming retired JSON.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite auth-store refactor and current runtime/test boundary history point to this owner for the migration-boundary decision.
